info.title: CommsHarbor
info.description: CommsHarbor API. Organization identity is explicit and tenant-scoped.

bearerAuth.description: Human session or scoped organization API key. Organization identity remains explicit.

description.description: What the product does, in one sentence.

base_url.description: Origin this API is served from.

ApiIndex.description: The self-describing index of the whole API.

ok.description: Always true when the Worker answers.

build.description: Deployed commit; CI passes the short SHA at deploy time.

Health.description: Liveness and the commit currently serving. Smoke tests wait for their own deploy here instead of racing edge propagation.

email.description: Email address confirmed by one-time code.

ok.description: Always true — failures arrive as a 4xx/5xx status, never as `ok:false`.

Ok.description: Write confirmation for an operation with no body of its own.

Profile.description: Personal preferences. They belong to the person, not to any organization.

id.description: Organization ID, used in every tenant route.

Organization.description: A tenant. Every piece of customer data in this product is scoped to exactly one.

userId.description: The person, when a session is in play.

email.description: The person's e-mail, on a session.

role.description: Role inside that organization; sessions only.

organization.description: `{ id, name, slug }` of the active organization; sessions only.

apiKeyId.description: Which key answered, on an API key.

scopes.description: Granted scopes; present on an API key, which carries its own narrower set.

Identity.description: Who the current credential resolves to. Read this before a write when you are not sure which organization is active.

Membership.description: One person's place in one organization.

invitation_token.description: The invitation token. Present only on the response that created it.

token_notice.description: Reminder that the token is shown once.

Invitation.description: An invitation into an existing organization. The token is revealed once, at creation, and never listed again.

id.description: API key ID, used to revoke it.

scopes.description: What this key may do, e.g. `crm:read`, `messages:send`.

prefix.description: Token prefix, so a key can be recognised in a list.

last_used_at.description: When the key last answered; null if never.

revoked_at.description: When it was revoked; null while it is still valid.

token.description: The key itself. Present only on the response that created it — it is never shown again.

ApiKey.description: A scoped machine credential. It determines its own organization and rejects a conflicting header.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

PageCamelAuditEvent.description: The same listing with the cursor in camelCase. Older resources ship it this way and the name is kept because changing it would break clients already reading it.

actor_user_id.description: Who did it; null when the actor was a key or the system.

metadata.description: Extra context for this action. Never contains recipient PII.

AuditEvent.description: One append-only record of something that happened in the organization. Audit is never rewritten.

ListaDomain.description: A complete, unpaginated collection — used where the set is bounded by design.

dkim_tokens.description: CNAME records to publish for DKIM.

dmarc.description: DMARC policy observed at the domain.

mail_from.description: Custom MAIL FROM subdomain and its observed state.

last_observed_at.description: When SES and DNS were last actually checked (UTC).

Domain.description: A sending domain. State is only ever what was OBSERVED at SES and DNS — this product does not infer it.

queued.description: Whether this call enqueued provisioning work.

job_id.description: The provisioning job, when one was created.

Provisioning.description: The idempotent SES provisioning queued for a domain. Asking twice does not provision twice.

ses_message_id.description: SES MessageId, for correlating with AWS.

Delivery.description: One queued message. It never carries the recipient address or the body — that is deliberate, not an omission.

remaining.description: Sends still available to this organization.

global_remaining.description: Sends still available across the whole platform this month.

hard_cap.description: The global monthly cap on real recipients. Nothing raises it.

Capacity.description: What is left to send. The bootstrap global cap always prevails over any tenant allowance.

queued.description: Whether a Queue message was produced.

job_id.description: Dispatch job ID, when one was created.

Dispatch.description: What actually happened to the queue message behind this send.

ListaDelivery.description: A complete, unpaginated collection — used where the set is bounded by design.

ListaDeliveryEvent.description: A complete, unpaginated collection — used where the set is bounded by design.

detail.description: Normalized detail for this event type, without recipient PII.

DeliveryEvent.description: A normalized SES feedback event. Open and Click are ADDITIVE — they never overwrite delivery state.

email.description: Email address, normalized and never truncated.

value_minor.description: Value in the currency's minor unit — cents, not dollars.

PageLead.description: Cursor-paginated listing. A null cursor means this was the last page.

source.description: Where the lead came from, e.g. `manual`.

stage.description: Where the lead is in our own funnel, e.g. `new`.

organization_id.description: The organization this lead became, once it converted.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

activity_type.description: What kind of activity it was, e.g. `note`.

marketing_enabled.description: Whether marketing may be sent to this contact right now.

source.description: Where the consent came from, e.g. a signup form.

unsubscribed_at.description: When the contact unsubscribed; null when they never did.

capacity.description: What is left after this send.

replayed.description: True when this was a replay of an earlier identical request.

basis.description: Declared consent basis for every row.

filter.description: The saved filter, for `saved_segment`. Only allowlisted fields are accepted.

Audience.description: Who a campaign goes to: a static list or a saved segment with an allowlisted filter.

variables.description: Typed variables the template declares: name, type and whether it is required.

blocks.description: Canonical content blocks. Imported HTML is converted into these.

latest_version.description: Highest published version; null while never published.

Template.description: An email template as a draft. Published versions are immutable and live in their own resource.

content_hash.description: Hash of the compiled content; it is the version's identity.

warnings.description: What was stripped or would not render — active content, forms, unsafe URLs.

mjml.description: MJML source of the compiled blocks.

PageCamelCampaign.description: The same listing with the cursor in camelCase. Older resources ship it this way and the name is kept because changing it would break clients already reading it.

scheduled_for.description: When it is scheduled, in the organization's timezone.

frozen_recipients.description: How many recipients were frozen at launch.

Campaign.description: A marketing send to an audience. Launching freezes the eligible recipients exactly once — the frozen set is what gets sent, no matter what changes afterwards.

events.description: Normalized feedback counts by event type.

CampaignReport.description: Campaign reconciliation: what was delivered and what came back. Counts only — no recipient data.

timezone.description: IANA timezone used to schedule campaigns, e.g. `America/Sao_Paulo`.

paused_reason.description: Why marketing was paused, when it was.

MessagingSettings.description: Timezone and marketing pause state. A reputation or SES tenant risk pauses marketing automatically, and resuming requires a healthy observation first.

ListaWebhook.description: A complete, unpaginated collection — used where the set is bounded by design.

event_types.description: Which events are delivered to it.

secret.description: Signing secret for timestamped HMAC-SHA256. Present only on the response that created it.

Webhook.description: An HTTPS endpoint that receives delivery events. The signing secret is revealed once, at creation.

payment.description: x402 configuration: network, asset, facilitator and where to pay.

invite_only.description: Whether new organizations require an invitation.

BillingPublic.description: The public billing view: catalog, x402 configuration and whether signup is invite-only.

version.description: Catalog version, so a client can tell prices changed.

trial.description: What a new organization gets for free.

pass.description: The paid pass: what it grants and what it costs.

topup.description: One-off send top-up: size and price.

checkout_live.description: Whether live checkout is enabled. While false, a purchase returns an x402 challenge.

global_recipient_hard_cap.description: Real recipients per month across the whole platform. This always prevails.

auto_renew.description: Always false — nothing here renews by itself.

BillingCatalog.description: Plans and prices, versioned. Nothing here auto-renews — a pass or a top-up is bought once and runs out.

provider.description: Always `x402` — the only billing protocol accepted.

mode.description: Seller mode: `live` charges for real, `dev` lets calls through unpaid.

network.description: USDC network: `base` in production, `base-sepolia` in staging.

chain_id.description: EVM chain ID of the network above, so the wallet signs on the right chain.

homolog.description: Staging seam on: the loop can be closed without spending USDC.

dev_gate.description: How dev mode is unlocked, when it exists.

facilitator.description: URL of the facilitator that verifies and settles the payment.

asset_address.description: USDC contract on the network above.

wallets.description: Links to wallets that speak x402 (metamask, coinbase, base_app).

PlanoX402.description: x402 payment configuration in force. Comes from `planPublic` and is the same across the products.

state.description: Current entitlement: what is active, how many sends remain and when it expires.

warning.description: Expiration or exhaustion warning, when one applies.

BillingTenant.description: What THIS organization is entitled to, and how close it is to running out.

alerts.description: Current alerts, each with a kind, a severity and what to do.

billing.description: Quota position at the time of the observation.

capacity.description: Conservative SES and SNS capacity observations.

Operations.description: Operational alerts for the organization — DLQ, backlog, worker and SNS failures, reputation, paused sending, quota and SES/SNS cost capacity. Never contains recipient PII.

ListaDataExport.description: A complete, unpaginated collection — used where the set is bounded by design.

DataExport.description: A tenant-scoped JSON export, retained for seven days.

scheduled_for.description: When erasure runs, after the grace period (UTC).

Deletion.description: A scheduled tenant erasure. It waits seven days, and what survives is pseudonymous financial and audit evidence only.

today_contacts.description: Contact messages today. Only with `METRICS_TOKEN`: contact counts never leave without the token.

days.description: One row per day of the window, with each metric's count.

usage.description: `entregas`: deliveries per day — real product usage, not catalog load.

financeiro.description: Day aggregate: `hoje_usd`, `hoje_count`, `rede`. Only with `METRICS_TOKEN`: money never leaves without the token; the full series is `payments`.

Metricas.description: 7-day operator dashboard. `payments` only appears with the token and only on Base mainnet.
